newsitem.title: URUGUAY: SOCCER-URUGUAY SACK COACH AFTER WORLD CUP DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-URUGUAY SACK COACH AFTER WORLD CUP DEFEAT.

text.p: Uruguay have sacked national soccer coach Hector Nunez in the wake of a defeat by Chile which left them in a sticky situation in the South American World Cup qualifying competition.
"They didn't give me specific reasons," said a perplexed Nunez after his dismissal on Thursday. "They told me it was over. Because of the results, I believe."
Nunez's dismissal came on the same day that Venezuela parted company with coach Rafael Santana, although in that case it was not clear whether Santana jumped or was pushed.

Tuesday's 1-0 defeat in Santiago left Uruguay seventh in the South American group, from which the top four teams qualify for the World Cup finals. They have won two games and lost three, the results including a shock home defeat by Paraguay.
But the contest is close and Uruguay are only two points behind fourth-placed Argentina.
"I think we were on the right track even though we didn't win in Chile," Nunez said. "There must have been pressures. I don't know what they were but it looks like there were influences."
Under Nunez, Uruguay hosted and won last year's Copa America, beating world champions Brazil on penalties in the final after a 1-1 draw.

However, the coach has since been strongly criticised for failing to make more of a talented squad. Players such as Gustavo Poyet and Marcelo Otero have been doing well with European clubs but have not been able to find their form while wearing the national team's sky blue shirt.
In September, Nunez virtually implored 35-year-old veteran Enzo Francescoli to come out of international retirement in a bid to save Uruguay's ailing World Cup campaign.
Uruguay were a major power in the early days of international soccer, winning the 1924 and 1928 Olympic soccer tournaments.

They hosted and won the inaugural World Cup in 1930 and won the competition again in Brazil in 1950, causing one of the biggest upsets in soccer history by beating the Brazilians in the final before an estimated crowd of 200,000.
But Uruguay have faded recently and they failed to qualify for the 1994 World Cup in the United States, losing out to Bolivia.
They have also earned a reputation for rough, defensive play, something the Uruguayans strongly reject.

Venezuela, on the other hand, have no soccer tradition and it is no surprise that they are bottom of the group with five defeats in six games. They have only ever won two World Cup qualifiers in their history.
